chapter_title: Concerning the Wheel and the Conduits
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly core mechanical teaching: a brief Q&A frame introduces a cosmological problem (wheel vs. conduits), followed by an impersonal explanation using analogies (ship/water; bird/air) to describe why pneumatic conduits are not cut or entangled. Only minimal dialogue attributions appear as later framing.

paragraphs.core_text: How does the wheel circle over the conduits, which extend from the heavens to the earths, and it not cut them? Or why shall the conduits not get entangled in with the wheel as it circles and drives [ ... through the u]niverse?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed Q&A frame/audience address: "His disciples say to him: Convince us, our master, about this other thing." This is hagiographic/dialogue attribution, while the remaining content is the substantive cosmological question that cues the old teaching topic.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue attribution and honorific address mark later framing, but the question itself is a technical cosmological problem-statement typical of the teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The reason that the conduits shall not be cut, for they are not cut, is because they are spiritual. Thus the conduits are like the waters through which ships sail. You shall find the prow that is in position in the front part of the ship divides the waters, casting them back and forth. So, when it parts the waters and that ship opens up the water with its cleaving prow, immediately and without delay the waters mingle with each other again behind the ship; and the path of the ship shall not be discernible in the midst of the waters.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution: "The enlightener says to them:" (a compilation frame marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core-style causal explanation of a cosmic mechanism (pneumatic conduits not being cut) with natural analogy; no institutional/ethical pivot. The opening speaker tag is the later Q&A container.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as when a bird flies up in the air, for its path is not visible in the air, and in the way of mankind, in the sun within the conduits. They also shall not be tangled up in them, and neither shall you find their path through the air known.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the mechanical analogy (bird/air) to explain invisibility/non-entanglement of paths—cosmos-to-nature explanatory mode without citations or church application.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the wheel. It turns through the conduits and the air. The wheel shall not cut the conduits, nor are the conduits themselves entangled in the wheel.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concise concluding statement of the cosmological rule (wheel passes through conduits/air without cutting/entangling), in impersonal explanatory voice.
